newsitem.title: UK: London gold and silver rises hit be selling.
newsitem.headline: London gold and silver rises hit be selling.

text.p: The gold and silver markets made a serious bid to move higher on Wednesday afternoon but were both being held by hefty selling around the 1500 GMT gold fix, dealers said.
"There were still plenty of specs (speculators) to cover (buy back) even after the past couple of days. We will see them start to cover if it (gold) established over $383.50," one dealer said.
Gold was fixed at $383.60 per ounce after $382.50 at the morning fix and $381.90 on Tuesday afternoon.
At the fixing, New York's Comex December gold futures contract advanced $1.40 to $384.80 in active business which saw funds covering against the rise met by profit-taking.
There was also some talk of producers selling metal into the rally, dealers said.
"There's been a lot of two-way business. There's a bit of a battle going on at these levels," one dealer said.
The historical price charts looked positive overall now that gold had broken out of its narrow $377-$381 price band.

"The $383.50-$384.50 is the resistance area. If it can get through $384.50-$385.00, the level from which it broke before, then it could get to $388.00-$390.00," a dealer said, adding that this was "a long way".
He added, "If there are any longer term speculators around still expecting a fall, then $385.00 is likely to be where they would come in and cover."

Silver, at $4.91/$4.93 up five cents, was finding selling at its $4.92 resistance, clearance of which could lead to $4.98. Dealers said there had been professional buying of silver earlier, suggesting positioning for a test of the resistance.
Platinum was steady but less active at $387.75/$388.75, unchanged, having been bought on the basis of Tuesday's report by refiner Johnson Matthey forecasting tighter supply this year.
"The widening platinum-gold spread also helped platinum as players started off short of platinum and holding gold, then had to buy platinum as the spread widened," a dealer said.
"That helped platinum and may have helped to cap gold as they sold off to buy the platinum," he added.
Palladium, which had did not pick up on the Johnson Matthey platinum-palladium survey on Wednesday, put on $2.50 to $120.25/$121.25 based on forecasts of higher demand next year.
